title: Curriculum learning
abstract: Proposes training machine learning models on examples ordered from easy to hard, in analogy to how humans learn, and argues that such a curriculum can speed up convergence and improve the quality of the solution found.

title: Self-paced learning for latent variable models
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
abstract: Introduces self-paced learning, where the model itself selects which examples to learn from at each stage based on their current loss, gradually admitting harder examples as training proceeds.

title: On the power of curriculum learning in training deep networks
abstract: Studies curriculum learning for deep networks with a scoring function that ranks example difficulty and a pacing function that controls how quickly harder data is introduced, reporting gains in speed and accuracy on image classification.

title: An empirical study of example forgetting during deep neural network learning
abstract: Shows that some training examples are forgotten repeatedly while others are never forgotten, and uses the number of forgetting events as a signal of example difficulty and importance.

title: Deep learning on a data diet: Finding important examples early in training
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
abstract: Proposes scores computed early in training, such as the norm of the error vector, that identify which examples matter most and allow pruning a large part of the data with little loss in accuracy.

title: Deep residual learning for image recognition
venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
abstract: Introduces residual networks, which learn residual functions with skip connections and make it possible to train much deeper convolutional networks for image recognition.

title: Learning multiple layers of features from tiny images
abstract: Technical report that introduces the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets of small natural images and studies feature learning on them.

title: Adam: A method for stochastic optimization
abstract: Presents Adam, a first-order stochastic optimizer that adapts per-parameter learning rates from running estimates of first and second moments of the gradients.
